name_reason: Conforms to fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>. '_46' is dispatch index 0x46 into the per-event handler table @ 0x51B91 (table entry @ 0x51CA9, (0x51CA9-0x51B91)/4 = 0x46), a meaningful domain ID, NOT a Ghidra address residual (function addr is 0x35B05; 0x46 is not its address nor a data address). 'ch28' = chapter 28 (valid chapter ID 01-30); 'dialog_with_state' is the handler category. Name accurately reflects the verified purpose. Matches the consistent naming of all sibling handlers in chevt2.c (handler_2f..handler_53).
purpose: Chapter 28 turn-event handler (dispatch idx 0x46, turn-event slot 2, turn=0xFF sentinel): disarms AI for a 5-char NPC range then plays a dialog + 3-portrait white-flash cutscene + dialog sequence.
logic_summary: Straight-line cutscene script (no branches, cyclomatic complexity 1): (1) fd2_set_combat_aux_block_byte_d_low4_for_char_range(0x29,0x2D,0) disarms AI control flag 0 for the 5 NPC chars 0x29..0x2D; (2) fd2_display_dialog_scene(current_chapter_text, page=5, 0xA0000, 0x140, 0xCD, 0x4C, 0x4A, 0x13, 1) shows dialog page 5; (3) three fd2_cinematic_chapter_portrait_dump_with_white_flash calls -- (8,7,3),(4,7,4),(0,7,5) -- a 3-portrait white-flash reveal (3rd arg = portrait-group/race selector 3,4,5, low byte only, not a chapter id); (4) fd2_display_dialog_scene page=6. In the binary the 3rd cinematic + page-6 dialog are reached by JMP 0x359FF, borrowing the alt_37 shared tail of fd2_chapter_event_handler_42 @ 0x359C8 (binary size optimisation); functionally exact source emits all 6 calls inline. Prologue is the Watcom __CHK(0x28) stack probe.
